title: The federal logbook, purchaser identification, record retention and logbook privacy for retail sales of scheduled listed chemical products
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.30(a) and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(iii), except for a purchase by an individual of a single sales package containing not more than 60 milligrams of pseudoephedrine, the regulated seller must maintain a written or electronic list of each scheduled listed chemical product sale that identifies the products by name, the quantity sold, the names and addresses of the purchasers, and the dates and times of the sales (the logbook). 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(iv) applies the identification and logbook-signature requirements in the case of a sale to which that logbook requirement applies. Under 21 CFR 1314.30(b) the regulated seller must not sell a scheduled listed chemical product at retail unless the purchaser presents an identification card that provides a photograph and is issued by a State or the Federal Government, or a document that, with respect to identification, is considered acceptable for purposes of 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(v)(A) and 274a.2(b)(1)(v)(B); the purchaser signs the logbook, for a written logbook by entering his name, address, and the date and time of the sale, and for an electronic logbook by signing a device presented by the seller that captures signatures electronically and displays the warning notice, a bound paper book carrying a printed sticker or a unique identifier linked to the sale information, or a printed document produced by the seller at the time of sale that is inserted into a binder or other secure means of document storage immediately after the purchaser signs; and the seller enters in the logbook the name of the product and the quantity sold. Under 1314.30(c), if the purchaser enters the name, address, date and time, the seller must determine that the name entered corresponds to the name provided on the identification and that the date and time entered are correct, and if the seller enters the information, the prospective purchaser must verify that it is correct. Under 1314.30(d) the seller must include in the logbook, or display by it, a notice that under 18 U.S.C. 1001 whoever, with respect to the logbook, knowingly and willfully falsifies, conceals, or covers up a material fact, makes a materially false statement or representation, or makes or uses a false writing or document shall be fined not more than $250,000 if an individual or $500,000 if an organization, imprisoned not more than five years, or both. Under 1314.30(e)-(h), the seller must maintain each logbook entry for not fewer than two years after the date on which the entry is made; records must be kept at the regulated seller's place of business where the transaction occurred, except that they may be kept at a single, central location of the seller if the seller has notified the Administration of the intention to do so by written notification submitted by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Divisional Office for the area in which the records are required to be kept; the records must be readily retrievable and available for inspection and copying by authorized employees of the Administration; and a record developed and maintained to comply with a State law may be used to meet the requirements of 1314.30 if it includes the information that section specifies. Under 21 CFR 1314.45 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(C) and (E), logbook information shall be disclosed as appropriate to the Administration and to State and local law enforcement agencies; it shall not be accessed, used, or shared for any purpose other than to ensure compliance with this title or to facilitate a product recall to protect public health and safety; and a regulated seller who in good faith releases logbook information to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities is immune from civil liability for the release unless the release constitutes gross negligence or intentional, wanton, or willful misconduct.
exam_relevance: Tests when a logbook entry and identification are required, the narrow single-package pseudoephedrine exception, who verifies what, the warning notice, two-year retention measured from each entry, where the records are kept, and the limits on disclosing logbook information.

exceptions: A purchase by an individual of a single sales package containing not more than 60 milligrams of pseudoephedrine is excepted from the logbook requirement, and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(iv) applies the identification and signature requirements only to sales to which the logbook requirement applies.

Records may be kept at a single, central location of the regulated seller instead of the place of business where the transaction occurred if the seller has given the Administration the required written notification.
A record developed and maintained to comply with a State law may be used to meet 21 CFR 1314.30 if it includes the information that section specifies.
common_confusions: The single-package exception is limited to pseudoephedrine, to a single sales package and to not more than 60 milligrams; a purchase of two such packages is not a purchase of a single sales package.
Staying within the quantity limits does not satisfy the separate logbook and identification requirements.
The two-year retention period runs from the date on which each entry is made.
